newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia studies Merukh's letter on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia studies Merukh's letter on Busang.

text.p: The Indonesian government said on Friday it is studying a letter from businessman Jusuf Merukh, who has filed a C$2billion lawsuit in Canada over the rich Busang gold find, offering a speedy settlement of the dispute, "We have received the letter and we are studying it," a source in the Mines and Energy Ministry told Reuters.
Merukh confirmed on Thursday that his lawyers had written to Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana requesting a meeting to explain his claims on Busang.
"We are willing to negotiate with Bre-X and the Indonesian government to reach a resolution of all outstanding issues," Merukh told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd has a partnership agreement with two companies controlled by Merukh in the central Busang zone, which is believed to contain some three million ounces of gold.

Bre-X estimates the entire Busang property, which includes the southeast and northern zones, contains at least 71 million ounces of gold -- making it the largest gold deposit in the world -- with a gross economic value of $24.8 billion.

He also questioned the validity of an agreement between Bre-X, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States, Indonesian companies PT Askatindo Karya Minerals and PT Amsya Lyna to jointly develop Busang.

Under the agreement, approved by the government last week, Bre-X will have a 45-percent stake in the property, Freeport 15 percent, Askatindo and Amsya and their partners 30 percent and the Indonesian government 10 percent.
"The (Mines and Energy) minister's announcement (accepting the agreement) has no legal standing," Merukh said. "In as far as I am concerned, there has been no agreement on Busang."

Merukh filed a suit against Alberta-based Bre-X following an ownership dispute between the two parties. The Indonesian businessman's claim he owns 40 percent of the entire Busang property has been dismissed by Bre-X as frivolous.
The suit is also directed at 19 other parties, including Indonesian and foreign companies.
"I am confident of getting what is mine. It's as simple as that," Merukh said. "There's nothing for me to worry about."
"My position in Busang remains unchanged. I own 40 percent of Busang," he said.
Merukh's four-page letter, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, outlines how gold was discovered in 1988, Bre-X's entry into the picture in 1993 and Bre-X's partnership with Freeport.
It said Merukh's PT Krueng Gasui had a 10 percent interest in the central zone, with an option to buy another 20 percent, while his PT Sungai Atan Perdana held a 10 percent stake.

"As you are aware, PT Krueng Gasui's strong desire is for Busang II and III to be amalgamated with Busang I, since this would restore to PT Krueng Gasui and PT Sungai Atan Perdana (what) is lawfully and rightfully theirs," the letter said.
"We are quite willing to negotiate with the relevant parties with a view to a prompt resolution of all outstanding matters in dispute," the letter said.
If this can be achieved, PT Krueng Gasui will not have to take further court action and barriers to the development of Busang will be removed, the letter said.
